name: Native Cowslip
grown_as: The wild cowslip, a hardy perennial of meadows and banks.
habit: A low rosette of leaves 10 to 20 cm across, sending up in spring one or more leafless, downy stalks 10 to 30 cm tall, each topped by a drooping cluster of flowers.

leaf.base: Narrows suddenly into a broad winged stalk (more abruptly than a primrose)
leaf.margin: Shallow, irregular, rounded teeth, the edge often crinkled or wavy
leaf.veins: A network deeply pressed in from above, raised beneath, making the leaf wrinkled
leaf.stalk: A broad winged stalk about as long as the blade or shorter

flower.form: A small cup-shaped bell that does not open flat, hanging from the top of the stalk
flower.petals: Five, joined into a tube; the five short lobes cupped, each with a small notch
flower.colour: Deep yellow with an orange spot at the base of each lobe
flower.centre: Five orange spots round a small throat
flower.behind: A large, pale green, inflated bell-shaped calyx with five short teeth, half hiding the tube
flower.carried: In a one-sided, drooping cluster (umbel) of 10 to 30 flowers at the top of a leafless downy stalk
flower.size: Each flower 1 to 1.5 cm across the mouth

fruit: An egg-shaped capsule inside the persistent pale calyx, which turns papery and straw-brown; the cluster turns upright as it ripens. Seeds small (1 to 2 mm), dark brown, angular and warty.
seedling: Two tiny round seed leaves, then small spoon-shaped wrinkled first leaves forming a rosette
winter: A small rosette of a few wrinkled leaves at the soil, or just resting buds in hard winters.

leaf: oblong-oval leaf narrowing suddenly into a winged stalk
bloom: small cup-shaped deep yellow flower, not flat
orange spots at the base of the lobes
seedling: first true leaves spoon-shaped and wrinkled
young: a low rosette of wrinkled oblong leaves
flower: a leafless downy stalk from the rosette
a drooping one-sided cluster of yellow cups at the top
seedhead: upright clusters of pale papery calyces on bare stalks
dormant: a small rosette of a few wrinkled leaves at the soil

look_alikes: Primrose (Primula vulgaris) has pale yellow flat flowers each on its own stalk from the rosette and leaves that taper gradually. Oxlip (Primula elatior) and the common false oxlip hybrid have larger, paler, flatter flowers without orange spots or with faint ones.
